trust_decision.summary: Untrusted Rows/Columns/BitsAllocated/NumberOfFrames from a loaded DICOM file decide how many bytes are copied out of the Pixel Data buffer; the decision that the buffer is long enough is made (or not) in each frame-extraction routine just before the memcpy loop.

landing_point.why: Summary names NumberOfFrames heap over-read and the first fix commit title is 'Fixed heap over-read in ConcatenationLoader'; ConcatenationLoader::extractFrames is the per-frame memcpy driven by NumberOfFrames. NOTE: at the pinned commit this site is already fixed (pinned commit == first fix commit).

fix_sites.entry_point: public API ConcatenationLoader::scan()+load() (also DcmSegmentation::loadConcatenation, dcmseg/libsrc/segdoc.cc:227-234); commit 1, ALREADY APPLIED at pinned tree
ConcatenationLoader::load() with BitsAllocated=1 (dcmfg/libsrc/concatenationloader.cc:251-253); commit 1 check present at pinned tree, commit 2 replaces it with the call passing getLengthField()
ConcatenationLoader::load() via computeBytesPerFrame (size_t promotion); commit 1, ALREADY APPLIED at pinned tree
public static API DcmIODUtil::extractBinaryFrames (dcmiod/include/dcmtk/dcmiod/iodutil.h:1005); commit 2 adds pixDataLen parameter and the length check; NOT applied at pinned tree
public API DcmSegmentation::loadFile/loadDataset (dcmseg/libsrc/segdoc.cc:185, 198) -> readFrames -> readPixelData; commit 2 passes getLengthField(); NOT applied at pinned tree

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: dcmiod/libsrc/iodutil.cc:715-754 (DcmIODUtil::extractBinaryFrames, public static, dcmiod/include/dcmtk/dcmiod/iodutil.h:1005) — no buffer-length parameter at pinned commit

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Every in-tree caller already validates the length first (dcmfg/libsrc/concatenationloader.cc:438-446, dcmseg/libsrc/segdoc.cc:1654 checkPixDataLength), so a solver can argue the utility is internal plumbing that needs no check and changing its public signature breaks API; for the O8 creator route: ConcatenationCreator is the writer/splitting side operating on the caller's own dataset, not a loader of untrusted files.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Correctly sized multi-frame data must still load, including 1-bit frames whose bit count is not a multiple of 8 (packed bit stream, last byte partial), Pixel Data padded to even length / longer than required (segdoc only warns), and 16-bit OW data where element count is words not bytes; an over-strict equality check or per-frame byte-rounding of binary frames would reject valid segmentations.

O6_input_shapes: BitsAllocated=16 (Uint16 array, count in words, x2 for bytes)
BitsAllocated=1 binary packed bit stream (ceil(rows*cols*frames/8) bytes)
Rows/Columns/BitsAllocated large enough to overflow int product (size_t promotion in computeBytesPerFrame)

O7_producer.where: Pixel Data element length comes from the dcmdata parser (DcmElement::getLengthField); no schema/serializer/cache producer involved

O8_uncovered_routes.route: ConcatenationCreator::writeNextInstance copies numFramesThisInstance frames from the source Pixel Data at offset derived from NumberOfFrames without ever comparing against the source buffer length; configureCommon's 'Check pixel data length correct' block checks only rows/cols/bitsAlloc.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Creator splits a dataset the application already holds (write side), advisory names the loader; pixDataLength is stored at dcmfg/libsrc/concatenationcreator.cc:533/546 so it looks 'handled'; also reachable via setCfgInput(srcDataset, pixelData, pixelDataLength) at dcmfg/libsrc/concatenationcreator.cc:89-128 where caller supplies the length.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package dcmfg, different file and class from the landing point

O8_uncovered_routes.route: ConcatenationCreator::configureCommon computes m_numBitsFrame = rows * cols * bitsAlloc in promoted int (same overflow the fix closed in computeBytesPerFrame), feeding the copy size and source offset above.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Only reachable with BitsAllocated=16 and Rows*Columns near 65535^2; the 4 GB per-instance cap at dcmfg/libsrc/concatenationcreator.cc:488-493 looks like it bounds it.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Parametric Map frame reader compares numTotalWords to numBytesFrame*numFrames/2 before memcpy; dropping or loosening that equality (e.g. to >= in the wrong direction, or for the Float/Double branches at :189-202) would be a realistic sibling.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Same per-frame memcpy pattern across three type-specialised readSpecific overloads; a maintainer adding the DoubleFloat overload could easily omit the check.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Enhanced CT frame reader with the same NumberOfFrames-driven memcpy; guard at :275 could realistically be absent in a copy.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Code is a near-duplicate of the dcmpmap reader in another package (second implementation at distance).

O8b_injection_room.sibling: getTotalBytesRequired ignores the return value of the 2nd and 3rd safeMult calls (ok not reassigned), so an overflowed bytesRequired could pass checkPixDataLength for 16-bit labelmaps.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Real, subtle arithmetic slip already in the code; a how-type sibling needing the size arithmetic understood.

O9_family: memory safety: heap buffer over-read (CWE-125) from header-declared frame count/geometry not validated against actual Pixel Data length

O10_build.toolchain: CMake (or autoconf Makefile.in) with a C++ compiler; DCMTK's own ofstd/dcmdata libraries
O10_build.project_tests: dcmfg/tests (t_concatenation_loader.cc, t_concatenation_creator.cc; OFTEST, needs data dictionary via DCMDICTPATH), dcmseg/tests/tutils.cc dcmseg_extractBinaryFrames; note t_concatenation_loader.cc NEMA test uses a hard-coded external path

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add a bytes-required vs Pixel Data length check only in ConcatenationLoader::extractFrames for 8/16-bit and stop, leaving the binary path, DcmIODUtil::extractBinaryFrames and ConcatenationCreator unchecked.
